entities.summary:
Paul Wolff Metternich was a Prussian and German ambassador in London (1901–1912) and Constantinople (1915–1916), a prominent German opponent of Ottoman actions during the Armenian genocide.

Born in Bonn, Germany, on December 2, 1853, Metternich was a member of the House of Metternich, a prominent aristocratic family in the German Empire. His diplomatic career spanned over three decades, with key positions including Ambassador to Austria-Hungary (1884–1886) and Ambassador to Russia (1893–1896).

Metternich's significance lies in his efforts to counter Ottoman aggression, particularly during the Armenian genocide. He played a crucial role in organizing international pressure on the Ottoman Empire to stop its systematic persecution of Armenians, and his diplomatic efforts helped to raise awareness about the atrocities committed during this period.

The legacy of Paul Wolff Metternich's work can be seen in the subsequent international responses to the Armenian genocide, including the establishment of the Armenian Genocide Recognition Project and the International Association of Genocide Scholars.

In the words of Paul Wolff Metternich, 'The fate of the Armenians is a matter of international concern, and it is the duty of the civilized world to take action to prevent such atrocities from occurring again.'

As a prominent figure in German diplomacy, Metternich's work had a lasting impact on international relations, highlighting the need for collective action against human rights abuses and genocide.
